touches.text: Postgres itself is a host service, installed and upgraded by Recovery (6.3.5); Rescue when it won't start.

A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (6.3.7.4). Node rows are the same on every box; the sync fills the blanks a box holds open (4.3.1.5.1.1). WHY: the local copy is fast, and the sync is the backup.

Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).
Other platforms get their own way to root (eg on Windows, Rescue and the installer run from an elevated PowerShell, 6.5.3.3).
Bringing Cairn to a new platform is a Rescue job, done on that platform (eg Windows, from inside an elevated PowerShell). WHY: Claude writes better Windows code on Windows.
Any shim, through its pulse.py, brings the bus up if it's down: whatever is called brings up what it needs (5.3.4.1).

A message nobody picks up within n milliseconds is pushed out of the buffer to the database, into a table that is just a table of messages. That table is the bus's exception to the memory model (4.3.1.5): it is not learning, and the buffer in front of it is what keeps the bus fast.

Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch().
